title: Blood Disorders and Blood Thinners: What the PCP Adds

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already control bleeding, give oxygen, keep patients warm and transport. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Link red cells, white cells and platelets to what you see on scene
  2. Recognize and manage sickle cell crisis, hemophilia and DIC
  3. Think through blood thinners: bleeding, pain relief, TXA

Textbook: Chapter 37, PDF pages 3198–3238
slides.say: Welcome back. Blood emergencies aren't common, but they can kill quickly. As EMRs, you already stop bleeding, give oxygen, keep patients warm and transport. As a PCP, you need to understand what is going wrong inside the blood, because it changes your questions, your drug choices, and your decisions about fluids and TXA, or tranexamic acid. Today we'll do three things. First, connect the three types of blood cells to what you see on scene. Second, recognize sickle cell crisis, hemophilia and DIC. Third, think through patients on blood thinners, including the BC rules for TXA.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。血液急症不常见，但可能很快致命。作为 EMR，你们已经会止血、给氧、保暖和转运。作为 PCP，你需要明白血液内部哪里出了问题，因为这会改变你的问诊、用药选择，以及补液和 TXA（氨甲环酸）的决定。今天讲三件事：第一，把三种血细胞和现场看到的表现对应起来；第二，识别并处理镰状细胞危象、血友病和 DIC；第三，想清楚服用「血液稀释剂」的病人怎么处理，包括 BC 关于 TXA 的规定。

slides.title: Three cell lines, three warning signs
slides.body:
Red cellscarry oxygentoo few → tired, short of breath, chest pain
White cellsfight infectiontoo few → fever, infection, sepsis
Plateletsstart the clottoo few → petechiae, nosebleeds, gum bleeding

Bone marrow makes the cells; the liver makes the clotting factors; the spleen filters out old red cells.
slides.say: Blood has three cell lines, and each gives its own warning when it runs low. Red cells carry oxygen. Too few is anemia, and the patient feels tired, short of breath, and may have chest pain. White cells fight infection. Too few, and the first sign is often a fever that can turn into sepsis. Platelets start the clot. Too few, and you see petechiae, tiny red dots on the skin, plus nosebleeds and bleeding gums. Remember the factories too: bone marrow makes the cells, the liver makes the clotting factors, and the spleen filters out old red cells.
slides.sayZh: 血液有三条细胞线，每条线不足时都有自己的警报。红细胞运氧，太少就是贫血，病人乏力、气短，还可能胸痛。白细胞抗感染，太少时最早的表现常是发热，可能发展成脓毒症。血小板启动凝血，太少就会出现瘀点，也就是皮肤上针尖大的小红点，还有鼻出血和牙龈出血。也要记住几个「工厂」：骨髓生成血细胞，肝脏合成凝血因子，脾脏清除衰老的红细胞。

slides.title: How a clot forms, holds and breaks down
slides.body:
platelet plug→clotting factors add fibrin→plasmin breaks it down later
  • Antiplatelets (ASA, ibuprofen, some herbs) weaken the plug
  • Anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin) slow the fibrin step
  • Clot-busters for MI, stroke and PE dissolve any clot
  • TXA works at the last step: it protects the clot

Ask about every drug: prescription, over-the-counter and herbal (ginkgo, garlic, ginger, ginseng, feverfew).
slides.say: To understand blood thinners and TXA, picture the clotting sequence. When a vessel is cut, platelets stick together to form a plug. Clotting factors then build fibrin strands that make the plug strong. Later, an enzyme called plasmin breaks the clot down. Drugs act at each step. ASA, ibuprofen and some herbs weaken the platelet plug. Anticoagulants such as warfarin slow the fibrin step. Clot-busters, used for heart attack, stroke and pulmonary embolism, dissolve clots, not only the bad one. TXA works at the last step: it protects the clot from being broken down.
slides.sayZh: 要理解血液稀释剂和 TXA，先想象凝血的顺序。血管破了，血小板先聚集成栓；接着凝血因子生成纤维蛋白丝，把栓子加固；之后，一种叫纤溶酶的酶会把血凝块分解掉。药物在每一步都能起作用：阿司匹林、布洛芬和一些草药削弱血小板栓；华法林等抗凝药让纤维蛋白这一步变慢；溶栓药用于心梗、卒中和肺栓塞，它溶解的不只是那个「坏」血栓。TXA 作用在最后一步：保护血凝块不被分解。

slides.title: Your PCP history: find the hidden problem
slides.body:
Unusual or hard-to-stop bleeding may be the first clue. Ask without judging: some patients hide a blood disorder.

Functional enquiryAsk and look for
Generalfatigue, fever, fainting, weight loss
Skinbruising, petechiae, pallor, jaundice, itching
EENTnosebleeds, bleeding gums, vision changes
GI / GUblack stool, blood in urine, heavy periods
Musculoskeletalbone or joint pain

Pale inner eyelids suggest low red cells (reliable only on normal-temperature skin).
slides.say: As an EMR you asked about history and medications. As a PCP you go further with the functional enquiry, the PCP-only system review in the BC assessment, and it's exactly how you catch a blood disorder. Ask about fatigue, fever, fainting and weight loss. Look for bruising, petechiae, pallor and jaundice, which is yellow skin. Ask about nosebleeds, bleeding gums, vision changes, black stools, blood in the urine, heavy periods, and bone or joint pain. A quick bedside sign: pale inner eyelids suggest low red cells, but only when the skin temperature is normal.
slides.sayZh: 作为 EMR，你会问病史和用药。作为 PCP，你要用系统问诊（functional enquiry）问得更深，这是 BC 评估里 PCP 独有的部分，也正是发现血液病的办法。问乏力、发热、晕厥和体重下降；看有没有瘀斑、瘀点、苍白和黄疸（皮肤发黄）；问鼻出血、牙龈出血、视力变化、黑便、血尿、月经过多，以及骨痛或关节痛。一个床旁小技巧：下眼睑内侧苍白提示红细胞偏低，但只在皮肤温度正常时才可靠。

slides.title: Anemia: not enough oxygen carriers
slides.body:
• Causes: blood loss, too little production, or fast destruction
  • Most common: iron deficiency from GI bleeding or heavy periods
  • Signs: tired, weak, "can't catch my breath", angina-like chest pain
  • High altitude makes it worse
  • Care: O₂ (high flow if SOB), frequent vitals, gentle transport
  • Go rapidly if LOC changes, BP drops or perfusion fails

The opposite, polycythemia (too many red cells), thickens the blood: stroke, DVT, PE, MI.
slides.say: Anemia means a low hemoglobin or red cell level. The most common type is iron deficiency, usually from slow bleeding in the gut or heavy periods. Patients feel worn out and say they can't catch their breath, and some get chest pain like angina, because the heart is short of oxygen. Give oxygen, high flow if they're short of breath, check vitals often, and transport gently, but go rapidly if their consciousness changes or the pressure drops. The opposite, polycythemia, means too many red cells and thick blood, so think stroke and clots.
slides.sayZh: 贫血指血红蛋白或红细胞水平偏低。最常见的是缺铁性贫血，通常来自肠胃慢性出血或月经过多。病人觉得精疲力尽，说喘不上气；有些人因为心肌缺氧，会出现像心绞痛一样的胸痛。给氧，气短就给高流量；勤测生命体征，平稳转运；但如果意识改变或血压下降，就改为快速转运。相反的情况叫红细胞增多症：红细胞太多、血液黏稠，要想到卒中和血栓。

slides.title: Low white cells: fever is an emergency
slides.body:
• Neutropenia: too few neutrophils, the main germ fighters
  • Classic call: fever after chemotherapy
  • Can become sepsis fast; infection signs may show late
  • Leukemia, lymphoma: fatigue, bleeding, bone pain, low BP, fast HR
  • Wear gloves and a mask: your cold could be fatal to them

Family only wants advice? Talk to medical control, document, get a refusal signed, and ask about their wishes if the patient arrests.
slides.say: Now the white cells. Neutrophils are the main cells that fight bacteria. When they're low, which is called neutropenia, the patient can't fight infection. The classic call is a cancer patient with a fever after chemotherapy. This febrile neutropenia can become sepsis very fast, and the usual signs of infection may appear late. Patients with leukemia or lymphoma may also have fatigue, unusual bleeding, bone pain, low blood pressure and a fast pulse. Protect them with gloves and a mask; even your small cold could be fatal.
slides.sayZh: 再说白细胞。中性粒细胞是对抗细菌的主力，数量低叫中性粒细胞减少，病人就无力抵抗感染。典型呼叫是癌症病人化疗后发热。这种「发热性中性粒细胞减少」可以很快发展成脓毒症，而常见的感染征象可能很晚才出现。白血病或淋巴瘤病人还可能有乏力、不明出血、骨痛、低血压和脉搏快。要保护他们：戴手套和口罩，你的一场小感冒对他们都可能致命。

slides.q: A 52-year-old finished chemotherapy 9 days ago. Her temperature is 38.3 °C and she says she just feels tired. Her other vital signs are normal. What is the best approach?
options: She looks well: advise rest and fluids at home
Treat it as a possible emergency: gloves and mask, full assessment, prompt transport
Give ibuprofen for the fever and reassess in an hour
Wait until she shows clear signs of infection before transporting
slides.say: Time for a question. A fifty-two-year-old woman finished chemotherapy nine days ago. Her temperature is thirty-eight point three degrees, and she says she just feels tired. Her other vital signs are normal. What is the best approach? A, she looks well, so advise rest and fluids at home. B, treat it as a possible emergency: gloves and a mask, a full assessment, and prompt transport. C, give ibuprofen for the fever and reassess in an hour. D, wait until she shows clear signs of infection before transporting. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你。一位五十二岁女性九天前刚做完化疗，体温三十八点三度，说自己只是觉得累，其他生命体征正常。最好的做法是什么？A 她看起来还好，建议在家休息、多喝水；B 当作可能的急症处理：戴手套和口罩，全面评估，及时转运；C 给布洛芬退烧，一小时后复评；D 等出现明确的感染征象再转运。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Fever after chemotherapy may be febrile neutropenia. Her immune system is suppressed, she can slide into sepsis quickly, and the usual signs of infection often appear late. A underestimates a dangerous situation. C only hides the fever, which is your best warning sign, and delays care. D is wrong because in these patients, clear signs of infection may come too late.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。化疗后发热可能是发热性中性粒细胞减少：她的免疫被抑制，可能很快滑向脓毒症，而常见的感染征象往往出现得晚。A 低估了危险；C 只是把发热这个最好的警报掩盖掉，还耽误救治；D 错在这类病人等到明确的感染征象出现，可能已经太晚。

slides.title: Sickle cell disease: a vicious circle
slides.body:
low oxygen→red cells sickle→small vessels block→even less oxygen
CrisisWhat happens
Painfulblocked vessels: clots, even stroke
Sequestrationthe spleen suddenly enlarges
Chestlung injury, severe hypoxia
Aplastica virus stops red cell production
Hemolyticred cells break down fast
slides.say: Sickle cell disease is the most common inherited blood disorder. An abnormal hemoglobin bends the red cells into a sickle shape. These cells break down early, causing anemia, and they get stuck in small vessels. That creates a vicious circle: low oxygen makes more cells sickle, they block vessels, and oxygen drops further. A crisis takes five forms: painful, from blocked vessels or even a stroke; sequestration, when the spleen suddenly swells; chest, with lung injury and severe hypoxia; aplastic, when a virus stops red cell production; and hemolytic, when cells break down fast.
slides.sayZh: 镰状细胞病是最常见的遗传性血液病。异常的血红蛋白把红细胞拗成镰刀形。这些细胞很早就被破坏，造成贫血，还会卡在小血管里。于是形成恶性循环：缺氧让更多细胞镰变，镰变细胞堵住血管，氧气就更少。危象有五种：疼痛危象，来自血管堵塞，甚至卒中；扣押危象，脾脏突然肿大；胸部危象，肺损伤加严重缺氧；再障危象，病毒让红细胞生成暂停；溶血危象，红细胞快速破坏。

slides.title: Sickle cell crisis: your care
slides.body:
• Often life-threatening: SOB, low BP, jaundice, pain anywhere
  • Oxygen breaks the circle; the book wants high concentrations
  • BC: high flow if short of breath or in shock; otherwise SpO₂ 94%
  • Rapid transport; PCP: IV and fluids under the BC protocol
  • High pain threshold: they often need more pain relief
  • Can mimic appendicitis or opioid withdrawal: don't judge
slides.say: Never take a sickle cell crisis lightly. Look for shortness of breath, signs of pneumonia, poor perfusion, low blood pressure, and jaundice, including yellow eyes. Oxygen is the key, because hypoxia drives the sickling. The book recommends high concentrations, and BC gives high flow to anyone short of breath or in shock. Transport rapidly. As a PCP you can add an IV and fluids under the BC protocol that fits. These patients often have a high pain threshold and need more pain relief. Their crisis can look like appendicitis or opioid withdrawal, so never label them as drug-seeking.
slides.sayZh: 镰状细胞危象千万别轻视。注意气短、肺炎征象、灌注不足、低血压和黄疸（包括眼白发黄）。氧气是关键，因为缺氧会推动镰变。原书建议高浓度给氧，BC 规定气短或休克的病人给高流量。快速转运。作为 PCP，你可以按适用的 BC 流程加上静脉通路和补液。这些病人痛阈往往很高，常需要更多镇痛。他们的危象可能看起来像阑尾炎或阿片戒断，所以绝不要给他们贴上「找药」的标签。

slides.title: Bleeding disorders: hemophilia and DIC
slides.body:
HemophiliaDIC
Causeinherited; A: low factor VIII, B: low factor IXsevere trauma with shock, sepsis, pregnancy problems
Dangerbleeding in the skull, often spontaneousclots everywhere, then bleeds everywhere
Cluesnosebleeds; blood in sputum, urine, stooloozing IV sites, purpura, bleeding into joints
Needsfactor and blood; fluid only buys timetreat the cause; death rate up to 75%
slides.say: Now two bleeding disorders. Hemophilia is inherited and mostly affects males. Type A is low factor eight, and type B is low factor nine. Bleeding inside the skull, often with no injury at all, is a major cause of death. Fluid can support the pressure, but what they really need is blood products and factor replacement. Even if the bleeding stopped before you arrived, advise them to be seen. DIC, or disseminated intravascular coagulopathy, follows severe trauma with shock, sepsis, or pregnancy problems. Tiny clots form everywhere and use up the clotting factors; then the patient bleeds everywhere. Some studies report death rates up to seventy-five percent.
slides.sayZh: 再说两种出血性疾病。血友病是遗传病，主要见于男性。A 型缺 VIII 因子，B 型缺 IX 因子。颅内出血是主要死因，而且常常没有任何外伤。补液可以撑住血压，但他们真正需要的是血制品和补充凝血因子。即使你到场时出血已经停了，也要建议他们去医院。DIC，即弥散性血管内凝血，发生在严重创伤合并休克、脓毒症或妊娠并发症之后：全身先形成大量微小血栓，把凝血因子耗光，然后到处出血。有研究报告死亡率可高达百分之七十五。

slides.title: Blood thinners change the call
slides.body:
• Same injury, more bleeding, often hidden (skull, belly, pelvis)
  • Ask which thinner they take and when the last dose was
  • Major bleeding? Call ahead so the hospital can get ready
  • TXA: trauma + shock, with visible, hidden or ongoing bleeding
  • A blood thinner is not one of the BC hard stops
  • Stops: allergy, over 3 h since injury, under 12, isolated head injury
slides.say: Many older patients take blood thinners: anticoagulants such as warfarin, or antiplatelets such as ASA. This changes the call. The same fall causes more bleeding, and it's often hidden, in the skull, the belly or the pelvis. Ask which thinner they take and when they took the last dose. If the bleeding is major, call ahead so the hospital can get ready. Now TXA. BC says consider it for a trauma patient in shock from blood loss, whether the bleeding is visible, hidden or ongoing. A blood thinner is not one of the four hard stops: a TXA allergy, more than three hours since the injury, age under twelve, and an isolated head injury.
slides.sayZh: 很多老年病人在吃血液稀释剂：像华法林这样的抗凝药，或像阿司匹林这样的抗血小板药。这会改变整个呼叫：同样一跤，出血更多，而且常常藏在颅内、腹腔或骨盆里。要问清吃的是哪种药、最后一次是什么时候吃的。出血严重就提前通知医院做准备。再说 TXA：BC 规定，创伤病人出现失血性休克时考虑使用，不论出血看得见、隐匿还是持续。血液稀释剂不在四条硬禁忌里；硬禁忌是：对 TXA 过敏、受伤超过三小时、未满十二岁、单纯颅脑外伤。

slides.q: A 74-year-old on warfarin fell down a flight of stairs 50 minutes ago. Her thigh is deformed, she has no head injury and no allergies, HR 122, BP 82/50. You have started the hypovolemia protocol. You are the PCP. What about TXA?
options: TXA 2 g IV over 1 minute, en route: she meets the BC criteria
TXA only after she has received 2 L of fluid
No TXA: it is only for penetrating trauma
slides.say: Here's a PCP decision. A seventy-four-year-old woman on warfarin fell down a flight of stairs fifty minutes ago. Her thigh is deformed, she has no head injury and no allergies, her heart rate is one hundred twenty-two, and her blood pressure is eighty-two over fifty. You've started the hypovolemia protocol. What about TXA? A, no TXA, because she takes warfarin. B, TXA two grams IV over one minute, en route, because she meets the BC criteria. C, TXA only after she has received two litres of fluid. D, no TXA, because it's only for penetrating trauma. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一位七十四岁、在吃华法林的女性，五十分钟前从一段楼梯上摔下来。大腿明显畸形，没有头部外伤，也没有过敏史，心率一百二十二，血压八十二比五十。你已经启动低血容量流程。TXA 怎么办？A 不给，因为她吃华法林；B 转运途中给 TXA 两克，静脉推注一分钟，因为她符合 BC 标准；C 等输完两升液体再给；D 不给，因为 TXA 只用于穿透伤。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. She is a trauma patient in shock from blood loss, she's within three hours of the injury, she's over twelve, she has no allergies, and this is not an isolated head injury. The BC TXA monograph doesn't list blood thinners as a contraindication or a caution, so A is wrong. C is wrong because nothing in the BC criteria makes you wait for two litres of fluid. D is wrong because the BC indication is about shock from bleeding, not about the type of wound.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。她是创伤病人，有失血性休克，受伤不到三小时，年龄超过十二岁，没有过敏史，也不是单纯颅脑外伤。BC 的 TXA 药物专论没有把血液稀释剂列为禁忌症或注意事项，所以 A 错。C 错在 BC 标准里没有要求先输两升液体。D 错在 BC 的指征看的是出血造成的休克，而不是伤口类型。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: bleeding in a blood disorder
slides.body:
BC Wound Care, Hypovolemia and Traumatic Brain Injury protocols; BC drug list

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Pressure → tourniquet → packing (never neck, chest, abdomen)
  • Supine, keep warm, O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Head injury: head of bed 30°, loosen the collar
  • Pain: acetaminophen, Entonox, methoxyflurane; check the stops
  • Ibuprofen: never with anticoagulants or GI bleeding

PCP adds

  • Functional enquiry (PCP only)
  • IV en route or if delayed
  • Fluid 20 mL/kg, max 2 L; reassess every 500 mL
  • TXA 2 g IV over 1 min, if criteria are met
  • Head injury: systolic > 120; glucose 4.0–8.0 mmol/L
slides.say: Let's put the BC rules side by side. We use three BC protocols: wound care, hypovolemia and head injury. On the left is what you already do as an EMR: bleeding control in the BC order, from direct pressure to a tourniquet to packing, but never packing the neck, chest or abdomen. Lay the patient flat, keep them warm, and give oxygen to ninety-four percent. Choose pain relief carefully: no ibuprofen with an anticoagulant. On the right is your PCP layer: the functional enquiry, an IV en route, fluid up to two litres, TXA when the criteria fit, and in head injury, a systolic above one hundred twenty.
slides.sayZh: 把 BC 规定并排放一起看。这里用三个 BC 流程：伤口处理、低血容量和颅脑外伤。左栏是你作为 EMR 已经在做的：按 BC 顺序止血，从直接压迫到止血带再到填塞，但颈、胸、腹绝不填塞；平卧、保暖、给氧到九十四。镇痛要选对：吃抗凝药的人不给布洛芬。右栏是 PCP 多出的一层：系统问诊、转运途中开静脉、补液最多两升、符合标准时给 TXA，颅脑外伤时收缩压维持在一百二十以上。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• ASA for chest pain: not with active GI bleeding or an ulcer
  • Methoxyflurane: not with significant kidney disease (e.g. myeloma)
  • Acetaminophen: not with severe liver disease
  • DIC or low platelets: IV sites may ooze; check them
  • Thinner + head hit only: no TXA; follow the head injury protocol
  • Recent transfusion? A reaction looks like anaphylaxis (first 30–60 min)
slides.say: Here are the new traps for a PCP. An anemic patient with chest pain may be bleeding from the gut, and BC says no ASA with active GI bleeding or an ulcer. Methoxyflurane is not for significant kidney disease, and multiple myeloma, a blood cancer, often damages the kidneys. Acetaminophen is not for severe liver disease. In DIC or with low platelets, your IV sites may ooze, so check them. A patient on a thinner who only hit their head gets no TXA; follow the head injury protocol. And if a patient was recently transfused, a reaction can look like anaphylaxis, usually in the first thirty to sixty minutes.
slides.sayZh: 下面是 PCP 要注意的新陷阱。贫血伴胸痛的病人可能正在消化道出血，BC 规定活动性消化道出血或溃疡不给阿司匹林。甲氧氟烷不用于明显肾功能损害，而多发性骨髓瘤这种血液癌症常损伤肾脏。对乙酰氨基酚不用于严重肝病。DIC 或血小板低的病人，静脉穿刺点可能渗血，要检查。吃血液稀释剂、只撞了头的病人不给 TXA，按颅脑外伤流程处理。病人如果刚输过血，输血反应可能像过敏性休克，通常出现在头三十到六十分钟。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Book: morphine for crisis pain → BC: no opioids for EMR/PCP
  • Book: IV fluids for many blood disorders → BC: IV is PCP only
  • BC bolus: 20 mL/kg, max 2 L, reassess every 500 mL
  • Book: blood products, PCC, vitamin K → not on the BC drug list
  • O₂: high flow if SOB or in shock; otherwise aim for 94%
  • TXA: 2 g IV over 1 min; four hard stops; a thinner isn't one
slides.say: For the BC exam, here's where the book and BC differ. The book mentions morphine for sickle cell and cancer pain; in BC, opioids are not in the EMR or PCP scope. The book gives IV fluids for many blood disorders; in BC, the IV is a PCP skill, and a bolus follows the BC numbers: twenty millilitres per kilogram, up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred. The book also discusses blood products, PCC and vitamin K; none of these are on the BC exam drug list.
slides.sayZh: BC 考试要注意原书和 BC 不同的地方。原书提到用吗啡处理镰状细胞危象和癌痛；在 BC，阿片类不在 EMR 和 PCP 的范围内。原书对很多血液病都给静脉补液；在 BC，静脉通路是 PCP 的技能，推注按 BC 的数字：每公斤二十毫升，最多两升，每五百毫升复评一次。原书还讲到血制品、凝血酶原复合物（PCC）和维生素 K，这些都不在 BC 考纲药物里。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Red cells low → hypoxia; white → infection; platelets → bleeding
  2. Sickle cell crisis: oxygen, rapid transport, real pain relief
  3. Thinners: hunt hidden bleeding; TXA by BC criteria; no ibuprofen

Next: Chapter 38, Environmental Emergencies
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: think in cell lines. Low red cells cause hypoxia and fatigue, low white cells cause infection, and low platelets cause bleeding. Fever after chemotherapy is an emergency. Two: in a sickle cell crisis, give oxygen, transport rapidly, and take the pain seriously, without judging. Three: blood thinners mean more bleeding, often hidden. Decide on TXA with the BC criteria: a thinner is not a hard stop, but an isolated head injury is. And no ibuprofen with an anticoagulant. Next time we start Chapter 38, environmental emergencies. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 最后记住三件事。一，按细胞线思考：红细胞低导致缺氧和乏力，白细胞低导致感染，血小板低导致出血；化疗后发热是急症。二，镰状细胞危象：给氧、快速转运、认真对待疼痛，不带评判。三，血液稀释剂意味着出血更多、而且常常隐匿。按 BC 标准决定 TXA：血液稀释剂不是硬禁忌，单纯颅脑外伤才是。吃抗凝药的人不给布洛芬。下节课开始第三十八章：环境急症。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
